text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Latvian foreign ministry denied Prime Minister Andris Shkele made any insulting remarks about Lithuanian officials as reported by Lithuanian business newspaper Verslo Zinios. The ministry also denies giving such an interview to the newspaper. The prime minister's press aide announced that Shkele rejected any connection with the statements in Verslo Zinios.

- Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans announced that the ministry allowed Aeroflot to resume flights to Latvia. The decision came in the hope that the Russian side will allow Latvian national air company Air Baltic to fly to Russia.

- The parties forming the parliamentary coalition of the Latvian Farmers Union have called on parliament to postpone amendments to the law on privatisation of rural land until after Novenber 1997, when the land market has been been put in order.
- 2,152 litres of alcohol worth $2.36 million were seized in Riga port by the mobile unit of the state revenue service.

- The director of the Latvian National Library presented the project of the library's new building to foreign ambassadors in an attempt to attract investments from their countries. The project is expected to cost about $50 million.
- The cabinet approved a draft law on private pension funds.
- Minister of Transport Vilis Krishtopans announced plans to visit Moscow on December 4-6. He will discuss cargo transit, including the transit of railway containers from China to Latvian harbours.
- On November 18 CNN broadcast an interview with President Guntis Ulmanis.
- Following the visit of President Ulmanis to the UK two British financial institutions are reported to have decided to create investment funds to invest some $40-50 million in Latvia.
- The Riga free port zone is expected to be dominated by off-shore companies.
